parsed.explanation: The combined regime shows no traveler-facing restriction: no criminalisation of gender expression, self-ID-based gender recognition (Ley 4/2023), facility access resting on self-determination, hate-crime aggravation applied in practice (Vigo 2026), and a prison sentence for gang violence against a trans person (Valencia 2026). Official travel advice, tourism certification, and documented high social acceptance corroborate. Deductions: one region repealed its non-discrimination law, conversion-therapy penalties and several recognitions (documented subnational exposure); attitudes more conservative outside major cities; violence statistics conflict and lack trans-specific rates; enforcement instances are few. No documented border, custody, or care exposure for visitors; no capital or custodial pathway for identity.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented border friction, marker mismatch scrutiny, or document-based outing of trans visitors.
entry_documents.protection: Foreign passport regime; official travel advice rates the country tolerant and progressive for LGBT+ travellers.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry screening interacts with national equality climate; no adverse rule documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented custody exposure for trans visitors; gender expression appears in no Criminal Code article.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Hate-crime aggravation (Art. 22.4) applied in 2026; prison sentence in gang assault case.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any police encounter would occur under a framework with bias-motive aggravation rather than identity-based offence.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: One region repealed its non-discrimination law, conversion-therapy penalties and several trans recognitions; visitors there lose that regional layer.
federal_state_facilities.protection: National Ley 4/2023 framework remains in force; facility access rests on legal gender self-determination.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor's itinerary into the dissenting region shifts the operative local framework while national law persists.

care_services.protection: Ley 4/2023 adds anti-discrimination measures in healthcare, employment and housing applicable nationally.
care_services.interaction: Emergency or routine care sought by an outed visitor falls under national healthcare anti-discrimination rules.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Historic dictatorship-era persecution (to 1988) and a 2013 ministerial hostile statement; conservative attitudes outside big cities.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Official and industry framing favourable; tourism institute certification of discrimination-free spaces; no free-standing gender-expression offence.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Historical hostility is dated; present official framing is protective.

minors_guardians.protection: Law regulates consent for medical procedures for minors aged 12-16; recognition from age 12 under conditions; two minors handled through juvenile process in the Valencia case.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family benefits from national protections, with regional repeals a residual uncertainty.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Valencia 2026 park gang assault and filming of a trans person; violence trend statistics conflict (4% down vs 7%/30% up) with no trans-specific rate or baseline.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Adult defendant imprisoned; observatory documentation shows recording and prosecution.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Sentence demonstrates functioning response, but limited case count leaves frequency uncertain.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Only two documented enforcement instances; applicability of aggravation elsewhere unsourced; regional repeals unremedied at national level.
remedies_unknowns.protection: First-instance application of the aggravation shows remedies operate; bias motive is a criminal-law aggravator.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists and functions in documented cases, but coverage outside major cities is thin.

anchor_checks.comparison: Far above: no entry-exclusion register, no universal state-imposed exclusion or humiliation for trans visitors; the documented machinery is protective (self-ID, hate-crime aggravation), not exclusionary.
Above: unlike Kestrel Isles' discretionary secondary screening and refused admission, no border friction, document-mismatch exposure, or administrative exclusion of trans visitors is documented here.

Similar but higher: like Meridia, border/entry treatment is respectful and remedies exist; this dossier adds stronger social acceptance, official tourism endorsement, and applied hate-crime enforcement, with fewer documented uncertainties.

Comparable: like Vessalia, protections are strong and remedies documented but enforcement instances are few and regional variation persists; here the regional repeal of protections is a concrete documented exposure lowering it slightly.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines a national self-ID framework (Ley 4/2023), facility access on self-determination lines, applied hate-crime aggravation, and positive official/social framing — with no traveler-facing restriction documented on entry, custody, or care. Deductions come from one region's documented repeal of non-discrimination and conversion-therapy protections (an itinerary-dependent exposure), conservative attitudes outside major cities, thin enforcement evidence (two instances), and conflicting undated violence statistics lacking trans-specific rates. The pattern sits in Low Risk: protections are not merely paper (court applied the aggravation; an assailant was imprisoned), and no tier-1 or tier-2 exposure appears for visitors, adult or travelling with a minor.
